mainTopic: בית שמאי and בית הלל on the order of ברכות over wine, the cup for ברכת המזון, and washing hands before mixing the cup.
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier point: a teaching that lets a person follow בית שמאי even after the בת קול fits רבי יהושע, who says we ignore a בת קול. The גמרא then challenges בית שמאי's rule that ברכת היום comes before the wine. A ברייתא about הבדלה puts the wine first. The גמרא proves that this ברייתא is really בית שמאי's, following רבי יהודה's report of their argument. It answers that בית שמאי treat bringing in שבת differently from taking it out: we bring it in as early as possible and take it out as late as possible, so שבת should not feel like a burden. Next it asks whether בית שמאי require a cup for ברכת המזון, and works through a chain of short questions about tasting the wine and the cup's minimum amount. A ברייתא of רבי חייא forces the conclusion that two תנאים report בית שמאי differently. Finally, the גמרא explains the argument about washing hands before or after mixing the cup. Both sides worry about impurity passing through liquid, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The teaching follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows following בית שמאי even after the בת קול fits רבי יהושע, who says we do not pay attention to a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this teaching follows רבי יהושע, who said: We do not pay attention to a heavenly voice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer from the previous lines. It explains how a ברייתא could allow someone to act like בית שמאי even though a בת קול announced that the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא asked how anyone may follow בית שמאי once a בת קול ruled for בית הלל. One answer is that the teaching comes from before the בת קול. This line gives a second answer: it may come from after the בת קול, but it follows רבי יהושע, who famously rejected a בת קול in the story of תנור של עכנאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A heavenly voice
We do not pay attention to it; we disregard it
The תנא who held that הלכה is decided by human sages, not by heavenly voices

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, according to רבי יהושע, הלכה is decided by the sages' reasoning and majority, not by signs from Heaven.

phrases.english: And it is (the view of) Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: That is, the ברייתא allowing one to follow בית שמאי follows his view.

phrases.english: who said: We do not pay attention to a heavenly voice.
phrases.notes: See בבא מציעא נט ע"ב, the story of תנור של עכנאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּבַת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of two answers to the earlier question about the בת קול. The question and first answer appeared on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed no one could follow בית שמאי after the בת קול ruled for בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע ignores a בת קול, so by his view one may still follow בית שמאי.

steps.title: A challenge: in הבדלה, the wine ברכה comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בית שמאי really hold that ברכת היום comes first. A ברייתא about מוצאי שבת puts the wine ברכה before הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית שמאי really hold that the blessing of the day comes first? But a ברייתא teaches: One who comes home on מוצאי שבת says the ברכה on the wine, then on the light, then on the spices, and after that says הבדלה. And if he has only one cup, he saves it for after the meal and says all of them, one after another, after ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בית שמאי's rule from the משנה that ברכת היום comes before the wine. It quotes a ברייתא where the wine ברכה comes before הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידוש, בית שמאי say the ברכה on the day first and then the ברכה on the wine. הבדלה is also a ברכה about the day, so we would expect it to come before the wine. Yet this ברייתא puts the wine first and הבדלה last, which seems to contradict בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה about the special day (such as קידוש or הבדלה)
Takes priority; comes first
But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
Saturday night, when שבת ends
Links them together in a chain, one after another

steps.confusionAlert: "After the meal" means the single cup is used first for ברכת המזון, and then the הבדלה ברכות are said on that same cup. The ברייתא is not telling him to skip הבדלה.

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
phrases.notes: This is really a challenge, asked as a question.

phrases.english: that the blessing of the day takes priority?
phrases.notes: As in their view about קידוש in the משנה.

phrases.english: But it was taught: One who enters his house
at the conclusion of Shabbat,
recites a blessing over the wine,
and over the light and over the spices,
phrases.notes: Note the order: light before spices. This becomes important in Step 4.

phrases.english: and afterward he says Havdalah.
phrases.notes: This is the main הבדלה ברכה, המבדיל בין קודש לחול.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד,
phrases.english: And if he has only one cup,
he leaves it for after the meal
and strings them all together after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי דְּבִרְכַּת הַיּוֹם עֲדִיפָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בת קול topic and starts a new challenge on the content of בית שמאי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's rule (from the משנה) that ברכת היום comes before the wine ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הבדלה is a ברכת היום, yet the ברייתא puts the wine first. If the ברייתא follows בית שמאי, they do not always put ברכת היום first.

steps.title: How do we know this ברייתא follows בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the challenge itself: maybe the ברייתא follows בית הלל, and then it says nothing about בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this ברייתא, how do we know it follows בית שמאי? Maybe it follows בית הלל!
steps.whatsHappening: Before trying to answer the challenge, the גמרא asks whether it is even valid. An unnamed ברייתא can only challenge בית שמאי if we know it follows their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא follows בית הלל, there is no problem at all, since בית הלל already put the wine first. So the challenge stands only if we can prove the ברייתא is בית שמאי's. The next step supplies that proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Perhaps; maybe

phrases.english: And this, from where (do we know) that it is Beit Shammai?
Perhaps it is Beit Hillel?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא, מִמַּאי דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי הִיא? דִּלְמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ברייתא quoted in Step 2 actually belongs to בית שמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the ברייתא in Step 2 follows בית שמאי and not בית הלל.

steps.title: מאור before בשמים shows it is בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא must be בית שמאי's, because it puts מאור before בשמים, and that order is בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that! The ברייתא teaches light and then spices. And who do we know holds this view? בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי by pointing to one detail in it: the order of light and spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists מאור first and בשמים second. That order belongs to בית שמאי, so the whole ברייתא is theirs. That means the challenge from Step 2 stands. The proof that this is בית שמאי's order comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; do not think that
Light (the הבדלה flame)
Spices
Reasoning; view

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
phrases.notes: That is, the ברייתא cannot be בית הלל's.

phrases.english: because it teaches light and afterward spices,
and whom have you heard
who holds this reasoning?
Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּקָתָנֵי מָאוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּשָׂמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 3 and so keeps the challenge of Step 2 alive.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא in Step 2 follows בית שמאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's order of מאור before בשמים, which matches בית שמאי's view (sourced in Step 5)

steps.title: רבי יהודה reports what בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה teaches that both schools agree ברכת המזון comes first and הבדלה last. They argue only about the order of light and spices: בית שמאי say light first, and בית הלל say spices first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught, רבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue that ברכת המזון comes first and הבדלה comes last. What did they argue about? About the light and the spices. בית שמאי say light and then spices, and בית הלל say spices and then light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא of רבי יהודה as the source showing that "light before spices" is בית שמאי's opinion. This completes the proof from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה narrows the argument: the beginning (ברכת המזון) and the end (הבדלה) are agreed on, and only the middle is disputed. Since בית שמאי alone put מאור first, the ברייתא in Step 2 must be theirs. The contradiction with בית שמאי's קידוש rule is now firmly in place. Step 6 tests this proof, and Step 9 resolves the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who reports the exact scope of the argument
They did not argue
Here: ברכת המזון, Grace after Meals
About what did they argue?

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge stands for now. A ברייתא that follows בית שמאי (we know because of the "light before spices" order) puts the wine before הבדלה. That seems to contradict their rule that ברכת היום comes first.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. In רבי יהודה's report, בית שמאי say מאור first and בית הלל say בשמים first. That is the reverse of the order many people assume.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehudah said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about the meal (blessing) being first
and about Havdalah being at the end.
About what did they disagree?
About the light and about the spices.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מָאוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּשָׂמִים,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: light and afterward spices,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּשָׂמִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָאוֹר.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: spices and afterward light.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind the claim in Step 4 that "light before spices" is בית שמאי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That "light before spices" is בית שמאי's order, so the ברייתא in Step 2 is theirs
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה describing the exact scope of the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא follows בית הלל according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from Step 4. Maybe the ברייתא is בית הלל's view according to רבי מאיר's version of the argument, not בית שמאי's view according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know it is בית שמאי according to רבי יהודה? Maybe it is בית הלל according to רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own proof. Putting light before spices might not be only בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version (Step 5), only בית שמאי put light before spices. But in רבי מאיר's version, which is our משנה, בית הלל also put the candle before the spices. So the order 'light, then spices' could fit בית הלל, and then the ברייתא would tell us nothing about בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
According to (the version or opinion of)
Perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: And from where do you know that it is Beit Shammai
and according to Rabbi Yehuda's version?
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה's version is the one quoted in Step 5.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is Beit Hillel
and according to Rabbi Meir's version!
phrases.notes: A משנה with no name attached follows רבי מאיר, so our משנה is רבי מאיר's version.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי הִיא וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the ברייתא made in Steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא must follow בית שמאי because it puts מאור before בשמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי מאיר's version, בית הלל also put the candle before spices, so that order does not prove the ברייתא is בית שמאי's.

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot match רבי מאיר's version at all
steps.stepSummary: In our משנה (רבי מאיר's version), both schools put the candle before מזון. The ברייתא puts everything after מזון, so it must follow רבי יהודה's version. In that version, light before spices is בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be. Our משנה teaches that בית שמאי say: candle, food, spices, הבדלה, and בית הלל say: candle, spices, food, הבדלה. But the ברייתא teaches: if he has only one cup, he saves it for after the meal and lines up all the ברכות after it. So learn from this that the ברייתא is בית שמאי according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by comparing the משנה with the ברייתא. Their orders do not match, so the ברייתא must follow the other version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version, both schools say the candle ברכה comes before ברכת המזון. The ברייתא says all the ברכות come after the meal, so it cannot fit רבי מאיר's version for either school. It must follow רבי יהודה's version, where both agree מזון is first. In that version, light before spices is בית שמאי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (that idea is impossible)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
He lines them up, one after another
Learn from this (conclusion of a proof)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different versions of the בית שמאי and בית הלל argument. רבי מאיר's version (our משנה) has the candle before מזון. רבי יהודה's version has מזון first for everyone. The proof depends on keeping these two versions separate.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for it teaches here in our mishna,
Beit Shammai say:
candle, then food (Grace after Meals), spices, and havdala;
and Beit Hillel say:
candle, spices, food, and havdala.
phrases.notes: In this version both schools put the candle before מזון.

phrases.english: And there, in the baraita, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד,
phrases.english: if he has only one cup,
he leaves it for after the meal,
and lines up all of them after it.
phrases.notes: Everything comes after מזון, unlike רבי מאיר's version.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it is Beit Shammai
according to Rabbi Yehuda's version.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּקָתָנֵי הָכָא בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 and restores the proof of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual comparison showing the ברייתא is incompatible with רבי מאיר's version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might be בית הלל according to רבי מאיר, since they also put light before spices.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the ברייתא puts all ברכות after מזון, it can only fit רבי יהודה's version. There, light before spices is בית שמאי.

steps.title: The contradiction about בית שמאי still stands
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא is proven to be בית שמאי's view, the original contradiction from Step 2 returns in full force.
steps.simpleTranslation: And either way, it is still difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: the defense is over, so the original question is back. This short line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say that for קידוש the ברכה of the day comes before the wine. But this ברייתא, which is now proven to be theirs, puts the wine before הבדלה. So בית שמאי seem to contradict themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: And nevertheless, it is difficult (the question remains)

phrases.english: And nevertheless, it is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 7 secures the identification, the גמרא returns to the challenge of Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's view that ברכת היום comes before the wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their own ברייתא puts the wine before הבדלה, which is the ברכה of the day on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: Bringing in the day is different from taking it out
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that we bring in שבת as early as possible, but we take it out as late as possible. That is why קידוש comes before the wine, but הבדלה comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that bringing in the day is different from taking out the day. When bringing in the day, the earlier we do it, the better. When taking out the day, the later we do it, the better, so that שבת should not feel like a burden on us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. Beginning שבת and ending שבת follow opposite rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ליל שבת, saying the ברכה of the day first welcomes שבת sooner. On מוצאי שבת, saying הבדלה last keeps שבת a little longer. Rushing to end שבת would make it look like a load we want to drop. So both rules come from one idea: showing love for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing in the day (start of שבת or יום טוב)
Taking out the day (end of שבת or יום טוב)
Better, preferable
A burden, a load

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית שמאי, we start שבת as early as possible and end it as late as possible. So קידוש comes before the wine ברכה, but הבדלה comes after it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a basic idea about how we treat שבת: we welcome it early and hold on to it late, rather than treating it as a burden.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold
that bringing in the day is different from taking out the day.

phrases.aramaic: עַיּוֹלֵי יוֹמָא, כַּמָּה דְּמַקְדְּמִינַן לֵיהּ עֲדִיף.
phrases.english: Bringing in the day: the earlier we do it, the better.

phrases.aramaic: אַפּוֹקֵי יוֹמָא, כַּמָּה דִּמְאַחֲרִינַן לֵיהּ עֲדִיף,
phrases.english: Taking out the day: the later we do it, the better,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֶהֱוֵי עֲלַן כְּמַשּׂוֹי.
phrases.english: so that it should not be on us like a burden.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי שָׁאנֵי עַיּוֹלֵי יוֹמָא מֵאַפּוֹקֵי יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the restated challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two cases (start of the day vs. end of the day)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי always put the ברכה of the day before the wine, so the הבדלה order is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה of the day comes first only when bringing the day in. When taking the day out, it is pushed to the end.

steps.title: Do בית שמאי even require a cup for ברכת המזון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בית שמאי hold that ברכת המזון needs a cup of wine. A משנה says that with one cup, בית שמאי bless on the wine first and then bench. That suggests he drinks the wine and benches without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית שמאי really hold that ברכת המזון needs a cup? But we learned: if wine came to them after the meal and there is only that cup, בית שמאי say he blesses on the wine and afterwards blesses on the food. Doesn't this mean he blesses on the wine and drinks it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The ברייתא assumed ברכת המזון is said over a cup, but a משנה seems to show that בית שמאי do not require one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had the person save his one cup for after the meal, which means ברכת המזון is said over it. But in the משנה, בית שמאי say to bless on the wine before benching. If he drinks it right away, no wine is left for ברכת המזון. That would mean בית שמאי do not require a cup for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires a cup (of wine)
But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? Introduces a contradicting source
Is it not that...? Introduces the proposed reading of the source

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
that Grace after Meals requires a cup?
But didn't we learn:
wine came to them after the meal,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ כּוֹס,
phrases.english: if there is only that cup there,
Beit Shammai say:
he recites a blessing over the wine
and afterwards recites the blessing over the food.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דִּמְבָרֵךְ עִילָּוֵיהּ וְשָׁתֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Is it not that he blesses over it and drinks it?
phrases.notes: If so, no wine is left for ברכת המזון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן טְעוּנָה כּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up an assumption in the ברייתא of Step 7 (saving the cup for ברכת המזון) and challenges it from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that בית שמאי require a cup for ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has בית שמאי bless on the only cup before benching. That implies he drinks it, so ברכת המזון would be said without wine.

steps.title: He blesses on the wine but sets it aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he blesses on the wine and puts it down, saving it so ברכת המזון can be said over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He blesses over it and puts it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading suggested in Step 10. The person does not drink the wine right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only tells us the order of the ברכות, not that he drinks right after the first one. He says the wine ברכה and then sets the cup aside. Wine is still available for ברכת המזון, so בית שמאי can hold that it requires a cup.

keyTerms.meaning: Over it
He puts it down, sets it aside

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's ruling to bless on the wine before ברכת המזון means he says the ברכה and saves the cup. It does not mean he drinks it, so ברכת המזון can still be said over a cup.

phrases.english: No, he recites a blessing over it and puts it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blessing on the wine first means drinking it immediately, leaving no cup for ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzMaskana: He blesses on the wine and sets it aside, so the cup remains for ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Whoever makes a blessing must taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 11. Someone who makes a ברכה must taste the wine, so how can he just put the cup down untouched?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say that one who makes a blessing must taste the wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11. There, the person said the ברכה on the wine (בורא פרי הגפן) after the meal and put the cup down without drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that whoever makes a ברכה over wine must taste some of it. If he puts the cup down without tasting, he has broken that rule. So the picture from Step 11 looks impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? (a formula that brings a known teaching to challenge something)
the one who makes the blessing
must taste

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
One who blesses must taste!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from Step 11 that he blesses and then puts the cup aside.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 11 that he blesses on the wine and saves it untouched for ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whoever makes a ברכה must taste. Putting the cup aside untasted breaks that rule.

steps.title: He did taste it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he did taste the wine. He just did not drink it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he tasted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: yes, he tasted a little. Then he saved the rest for ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 never meant that he left the wine completely untouched. He tasted, which satisfies the rule. Then he kept the cup for benching.

keyTerms.meaning: he tasted it

phrases.english: Where he tasted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by adding that he tasted the wine.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case (he tasted, but did not finish the cup).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saving the cup meant not tasting it at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He tasted a little and saved the rest.

steps.title: Tasting spoils the cup
steps.stepSummary: If he tasted from the cup, he spoiled it. Then it can no longer be used as a כוס של ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: if he tasted it, he damaged it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 13. If he tasted from the cup, it becomes unfit to use for ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule called טעמו פגמו. Once someone drinks from a cup, it counts as 'damaged' and cannot be used for a ברכה. So tasting solves one problem but creates another.

keyTerms.meaning: if he tasted it, he damaged it (made it unfit for a ברכה)

steps.confusionAlert: פגום here does not mean the wine went bad. It means that drinking from the cup makes it unfit to be used for a ברכה.

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
If he tasted it, he damaged it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that he tasted from the cup.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tasting makes the cup פגום, so it can no longer serve for ברכת המזון.

steps.title: He tasted from his hand
steps.stepSummary: He poured a little wine into his hand and tasted from there. The cup itself stays undamaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: He tasted it from his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he did not drink from the cup itself. He poured some wine into his hand and tasted that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of פגום applies only to drinking straight from the cup. Tasting wine poured out into his hand fulfills the need to taste. The cup stays fit for a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: with his hand

phrases.english: Where he tasted it with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by explaining exactly how he tasted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He tasted from the cup itself and damaged it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He tasted from wine poured into his hand, so the cup stays undamaged.

steps.title: Tasting lowers the required amount
steps.stepSummary: A כוס של ברכה needs a minimum amount of wine. Pouring some out to taste would leave less than that amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say that a cup of blessing needs a set amount? By taking some out, he lowers it below that amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15. Pouring wine out of the cup leaves less than the required amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוס של ברכה must hold a minimum שיעור of wine. Even if the cup is not damaged, taking wine out for tasting leaves it too small. So the cup still cannot be used for ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: the cup of wine used for a ברכה, like ברכת המזון
the minimum required amount
lowers, reduces

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
A cup of blessing requires a set amount,
and here he reduces it below its amount!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר מָר כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ שִׁעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Tasting by pouring wine into his hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking wine out leaves the cup below the required amount.

steps.title: The cup had extra wine
steps.stepSummary: The cup held more than the minimum amount, so tasting a little still leaves enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where it held more than its required amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cup was fuller than the minimum. After tasting, enough wine was still left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cup had more than the שיעור, removing a little for tasting does not bring it below the minimum. So the cup still works for ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: is a lot, has more
more

phrases.english: Where it had more than its required amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by describing a fuller cup.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cup held exactly the minimum, so tasting would ruin it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cup held extra, so tasting leaves enough.

steps.title: But the משנה said only one cup
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a person who has only one cup. A cup with extra wine sounds like more than one cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: 'If there is only that one cup'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 17 using the wording of the משנה, which speaks of someone who has only one cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he had extra wine beyond one cup, then he did not really have 'only one cup.' The answer from Step 17 seems to clash with the משנה's own wording.

keyTerms.term: אִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ כּוֹס
keyTerms.meaning: if there is only that one cup
it teaches

phrases.english: But 'if there is not there'
'anything but that one cup' is what it teaches!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ כּוֹס קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 17 from the משנה's wording, which was quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the cup held more than the required amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'only one cup', and extra wine contradicts that.

steps.title: More than one cup but less than two
steps.stepSummary: He has more than one cup's worth of wine but not enough for two cups. So it still counts as 'only one cup.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There are not two, but it is more than one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he has a little extra wine. It is not enough to make a second cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Only one cup' means he does not have enough for two separate cups. A cup with a small extra amount fits that description. It also has enough to taste and still keep the שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not two
it is more than one

phrases.english: It is not two,
but it is more than one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by reading 'only one cup' as 'less than two.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Only one cup' means exactly one minimum-size cup.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Only one cup' means not enough for two, even if there is a little extra.

steps.title: רבי חייא: בית שמאי drink the wine and then bench
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי חייא says plainly that בית שמאי drink the wine and then bench. That means no cup is saved for ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא taught: בית שמאי say, he blesses on the wine and drinks it, and afterward he says ברכת המזון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new and stronger challenge from a ברייתא taught by רבי חייא. It openly says that the wine is drunk before benching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11–19 worked hard to show that the wine was saved for ברכת המזון. But רבי חייא's version says outright 'he drinks it.' This cannot be explained away, so according to this ברייתא, בית שמאי do not require a cup for benching.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי חייא taught (in a ברייתא)
and drinks it

phrases.english: But didn't רבי חייא teach:
בית שמאי say:
he blesses on the wine and drinks it,
and afterward he says Grace after Meals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the run of small answers. It brings an explicit source that contradicts the whole approach of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from Step 11 that בית שמאי save the cup for ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's ברייתא says explicitly that he drinks it, so no wine is saved for ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that two תנאים report בית שמאי's view differently. One version requires a cup for ברכת המזון, and one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, these are two תנאים, and they disagree about what בית שמאי held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops trying to make the sources match. It says the two sources reflect two different reports of בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, as explained in Step 11, holds that בית שמאי require a cup for ברכת המזון. רבי חייא's ברייתא holds that they do not. Since the explicit ברייתא cannot be explained away, the גמרא admits a real disagreement among תנאים about בית שמאי's position.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier approach)
two תנאים who disagree
according to (the view of)

steps.whatToRemember: With only one cup after the meal, בית שמאי say the ברכה on the wine first and then ברכת המזון. Whether they also need that cup for ברכת המזון is itself a disagreement between two תנאים who report בית שמאי's view.

phrases.english: Rather, these are two tannaim,
and they disagree regarding the view of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 20 and settles it by saying two תנאים disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תרי תנאי: assigning the sources to two different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sources agree on one view of בית שמאי, so the wine must be saved for ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים report בית שמאי differently. One requires a cup for ברכת המזון, and one does not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether בית שמאי require a cup of wine for ברכת המזון depends on which תנא's report of their view you follow.

steps.title: Quoting the next part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the next clause of the משנה, where בית שמאי state their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בית שמאי say,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares us to explain בית שמאי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה is: בית שמאי say you wash your hands and then mix the cup, while בית הלל say you mix the cup and then wash. The 'וכו׳' tells us to remember that whole line. The next step will bring a ברייתא explaining בית שמאי's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' A sign that only the opening words of a longer source are being quoted.
The school of Shammai's students, who often disagree with בית הלל.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the earlier argument about which ברכה comes first (the day or the wine). This is a new argument in the same משנה, about whether washing hands or mixing the cup comes first.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say, etc.
phrases.notes: Points to the משנה: wash hands first, then mix the cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the cup for ברכת המזון and opens the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, washing the hands comes before mixing the cup.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains why בית שמאי wash first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that בית שמאי require washing first. Otherwise, unwashed hands might make the liquid on the outside of the cup impure, and that liquid would then make the cup impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בית שמאי say you wash your hands and afterward mix the cup. If you say to mix the cup first, there is a decree out of concern that the liquid on the outside of the cup will become impure because of his hands, and that liquid will then make the cup impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the reason behind בית שמאי's rule. The concern is a chain of impurity, from the hands to the liquid to the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unwashed hands are treated as impure by rabbinic law. When you pour and mix wine, drops land on the outside of the cup. If your hands are still unwashed, they touch those drops and make them impure, and the impure drops then make the cup impure. Washing first prevents the whole chain.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands (נטילת ידיים).
Mixing the cup, meaning adding water to the strong wine.
A rabbinic decree made as a protective measure.
The liquid on the outside (back) of the cup.
Ritual impurity.

steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets up the puzzle for the next two steps: why does the ברייתא need the liquid in the middle of the chain at all?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Beit Shammai say:
One washes the hands
and afterward mixes the cup,
for if you say
that one mixes the cup first,
there is a decree, lest there become impure
the liquids that are on the outside of the cup
because of his hands,
phrases.notes: His hands are still unwashed, and so impure.

phrases.english: and they will in turn make the cup impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the משנה line quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wash first, so that unwashed hands do not make the liquid on the cup impure, which would in turn make the cup impure.

steps.title: Why not say the hands make the cup impure directly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs the liquid in the middle. The hands could simply make the cup impure themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the hands make the cup impure directly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It seems to describe an extra, unnecessary step in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hands touch the cup anyway when you mix the wine. If impure hands can make things impure, the simple worry should be 'hands make the cup impure.' Bringing in the liquid on the outside of the cup seems like a pointless detour.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But let them make impure.' A challenge that suggests a simpler explanation.

phrases.english: But let the hands make the cup impure (directly)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the chain of impurity described in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the impurity reaches the cup through the liquid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hands touch the cup directly, so the liquid seems unnecessary. The ברייתא should have said the hands make the cup impure.

steps.title: Hands are second level and need liquid to pass on impurity
steps.stepSummary: Hands are only at the second level of impurity (שני). Something at the second level cannot make ordinary items (חולין) impure, unless liquids are involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hands are at the second level of impurity. Something at the second level cannot make ordinary (non-holy) items impure at a third level, except through liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the rules of impurity levels. The hands cannot make the cup impure on their own. That is why the liquid has to be in the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unwashed hands have the status of שני (second level). For ordinary items (חולין), impurity stops at the second level, so a שני cannot create a שלישי by itself. Liquids are different: the חכמים decreed that liquid touching a שני becomes impure at a stronger level, so the liquid can make the cup impure. That is exactly why the ברייתא mentions the liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: At the second level of impurity (from שֵׁנִי לְטֻמְאָה).
A second-level item creating a third-level item, meaning passing impurity one step further.
Ordinary, non-holy food and items, unlike תרומה or קדשים.
Through liquids. Liquids are the exception that can pass impurity onward.

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי wash first because of a chain of impurity: unwashed hands (שני) make the liquid on the outside of the cup impure, and the liquid makes the cup impure. The hands alone cannot make a חולין cup impure, because a שני cannot create a שלישי in חולין without liquids.
steps.confusionAlert: It can seem strange that the hands cannot make the cup impure directly, yet they can do it by way of liquid. The key is that liquids are a special case. They pick up impurity at a stronger level, so they can pass it on even when the hands cannot.

phrases.english: Hands are at the second level (of impurity),
and a second-level item cannot create a third level in ordinary (non-holy) items
except by means of liquids.
phrases.notes: Liquids touching a שני become impure at a stronger level and can make the cup impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 and defends the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a rule of impurity levels that shows why the extra step in the ברייתא is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hands could make the cup impure directly, so the liquid seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hands are שני and cannot make a חולין cup impure. Only through the liquid does the impurity reach the cup.

steps.title: בית הלל: Mix the cup first, then wash hands
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives בית הלל's view: mix the cup first, then wash. If you wash first, the wet hands might touch an impure cup, the liquid on the hands would become impure, and that liquid would make the hands impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: You mix the cup first and afterward wash your hands. Because if you say to wash the hands first, there is a rabbinic decree. We worry that the liquid on the hands will become impure because of the cup, and that liquid will then turn around and make the hands impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side, בית הלל's order and the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of בית שמאי's worry. בית שמאי feared the hands would harm the cup. בית הלל fear that the cup, whose outside may be impure, will harm the clean hands. The harm passes through the liquid left on the hands after washing.

keyTerms.meaning: mixing the cup (adding water to the wine)
ritual washing of the hands
a rabbinic decree made to prevent a problem
the liquid left on the hands after washing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. In בית שמאי's view, the hands make the cup impure. In בית הלל's view, the cup makes the hands impure. In both views, liquid is the middleman.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
One mixes the cup
and afterward washes the hands.
For if you say
one washes the hands first,
there is a decree, lest they become impure:
the liquid on the hands, because of the cup,
phrases.notes: The cup's outside may be impure.

phrases.english: and it will turn around and make the hands impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מוֹזְגִין אֶת הַכּוֹס וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 23, now giving בית הלל's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mix the cup first, then wash. Otherwise the cup may make the liquid on the hands impure, and that liquid would make the hands impure.

steps.title: Why not let the cup make the hands impure directly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the liquid is needed in the middle. The cup could simply make the hands impure itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the cup make the hands impure directly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's chain. Why go through the liquid, if the cup could touch the hands directly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels the question in Step 24, but in the opposite direction. If the cup is impure, the ברייתא should have said the cup itself makes the hands impure.

keyTerms.meaning: so let it make impure (a challenging question)

phrases.english: Let the cup make the hands impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the liquid-middleman reasoning of Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for liquid between the cup and the hands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cup is impure and touches the hands, it should be able to make them impure without any liquid.

steps.title: A vessel cannot make a person impure
steps.stepSummary: A כלי does not make a person impure. So the cup cannot affect the hands directly, and the liquid is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel does not make a person impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a basic rule: a vessel cannot pass impurity to a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person becomes impure only from a strong source of impurity, an אב הטומאה. A cup like this is not such a source. So the only way the hands can become impure is through liquid, because liquid easily picks up impurity and passes it on.

keyTerms.meaning: a vessel does not make a person impure
a primary source of impurity, strong enough to make a person impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why liquid plays the middleman role in both בית שמאי's and בית הלל's reasoning.

phrases.english: A vessel does not make a person impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a general rule of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cup can make the hands impure directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vessel cannot make a person impure, so the liquid is needed as a middleman.

steps.title: Why isn't the wine inside the cup impure too?
steps.stepSummary: If the cup is impure, it should make the wine inside it impure. Then the whole cup would be unusable anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the cup make the liquid inside it impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. An impure cup should make its own wine impure, so why only worry about the hands?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cup is impure, the wine inside it would also be ruined. Then the order of washing would hardly matter. The question pushes the גמרא to define exactly what kind of impure cup we are discussing.

keyTerms.meaning: the liquid inside the cup

phrases.english: Let it make the liquid inside it impure!

steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that only the hands are at risk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An impure cup should ruin its own wine, so the worry about the hands seems beside the point.

steps.title: Only the outside of the cup is impure
steps.stepSummary: The case is a cup whose outside alone became impure through liquids. Its inside stays pure, so the wine is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a vessel whose outside became impure through liquids. Its inside is pure and its outside is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. Only the back of the cup is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When impure liquids touch only the outside of a כלי, the rabbis declared only the outside impure, not the inside. So the wine inside is not affected. But the hands, which touch the outside, can still be affected through the liquid on them.

steps.title: A משנה supports this: only the outside is impure
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that when liquids make the outside of a vessel impure, only the outside is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A vessel whose outside became impure through liquids, its outside is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as a source for the idea that the inside and outside of a vessel can have different statuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה confirms that impurity on the back of a vessel through liquids stays on the back. The quote continues on the next amud, which lists the parts that stay pure.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: mix first, then wash. The worry is an impure cup making the liquid on the hands impure, which then makes the hands impure. A כלי cannot make a person impure directly. Only the outside of this cup is impure, so the wine inside is fine.
